title: Identification and multiply robust estimation in causal mediation analysis across principal strata
headline: Open finding: The cross-fitted nonparametric estimator is consistent when any three of four nuisance groups are consistently estimated under Assumptions 1-6.

work.title: Identification and multiply robust estimation in causal mediation analysis across principal strata
work.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

claims.label: Theorem 5 first consistency clause
claims.gist: The cross-fitted nonparametric estimator is consistent when any three of four nuisance groups are consistently estimated under Assumptions 1-6.
claims.statement: The cross-fitted nonparametric estimator is consistent when any three of four nuisance groups are consistently estimated under Assumptions 1-6.
conditions: Any three nuisance groups are consistently estimated; the fourth may be misspecified.
claims.quantifiers: All fold-specific learners satisfying the printed conditions.

result.summary: With three nuisances exactly correct and the fourth equal to sqrt(n), the cross-fitted score fails to concentrate and the estimator converges in distribution to N(0,1) rather than to zero.
result.witness: With three nuisances exactly correct and the fourth equal to sqrt(n), the cross-fitted score fails to concentrate and the estimator converges in distribution to N(0,1) rather than to zero.
result.argument: Exact score substitution, square-root-n nuisance witness, numerator/denominator limits, rescue attempts and minimal stability repair. Limits: Population multiple robustness, identification, Theorem 4 and the all-nuisances-consistent asymptotic-normality clause are not challenged.
not_claimed: This is plausibly an omitted-hypothesis defect rather than failure of the intended stable-learner theorem.

vor_check.detail: Source verification is at the canonical partial level; the record does not overstate Version of Record verification.

evidence.detail: A fresh separate-session hostile validation supports the stated finding; its scope and limits are summarized above.
